# openobserve_pipelines (Data Source)

Lists the pipelines in an organization.

This is the fastest way to find the `pipeline_id` a `terraform import` needs, since a pipeline's identifier is server-assigned and not visible in configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "openobserve_pipelines" "all" {}

# A pipeline's identifier is server-assigned, so this is the fastest way to find
# the id a `terraform import` needs.
output "pipeline_ids" {
  value = { for p in data.openobserve_pipelines.all.pipelines : p.name => p.pipeline_id }
}

output "paused_pipelines" {
  value = [for p in data.openobserve_pipelines.all.pipelines : p.name if !p.enabled]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source ID, the organization identifier.
- `pipelines` (Attributes List) Every pipeline in the organization. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pipelines))

<a id="nestedatt--pipelines"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pipelines`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) What the pipeline does.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether it is processing records.
- `name` (String) Pipeline name, as the server stored it.
- `node_count` (Number) How many nodes the graph has.
- `pipeline_id` (String) Server-assigned identifier, which is what `terraform import` takes.
- `source_type` (String) `realtime` or `scheduled`.
- `stream_name` (String) Source stream, for a realtime pipeline.
- `stream_type` (String) Type of the source stream.
